A_6_1.title: Screening
A_6_1.description: Before hiring, the company checks candidates' backgrounds as far as the law allows and the role justifies, for example certificates or references.

A_6_2.title: Terms and Conditions of Employment
A_6_2.description: Agreements with employees and contractors state their responsibilities and the company's for information security.

A_6_3.title: Information Security Awareness, Education and Training
A_6_3.description: Staff learn the security rules and risks that matter for their work, and people with special tasks get deeper training. Recommendation: train new staff when they join and everyone once a year.

A_6_4.title: Disciplinary Process
A_6_4.description: The company has a known, fair process for dealing with breaches of the security rules.

A_6_5.title: Responsibilities After Termination or Change of Employment
A_6_5.description: Security duties that continue after someone leaves or changes role, such as confidentiality, are agreed and communicated.

A_6_6.title: Confidentiality or Non-Disclosure Agreements
A_6_6.description: The company decides where confidentiality agreements are needed, uses them with staff and outside parties, and keeps them current.

A_6_7.title: Remote Working
A_6_7.description: Rules and technical measures protect information when staff work from home or on the road, for example secure connections and privacy screens.

A_6_8.title: Information Security Event Reporting
A_6_8.description: Staff have a simple way to report security events or weaknesses they notice, and know that they should use it.
